text:
maya: quick flag — noticed a p95 latency bump on the KV-heavy endpoint during the long-running perf test last night. looks correlated with sustained long sequences + many pinned KV entries.

ash: ugh. which test? the 512-token conversation sim or the streaming regen load?

maya: 512 conv sim, steady rps ~280, tail jumps from 110ms -> 220ms for ~3 minutes then recovers.

perf-bot: [auto] perf-regression-detect: KV pressure detected on node r-13b-02; memory headroom dropped below 8%. Attach: flamegraph_3058765432.svg

darren: can you paste the profiler output? curious if kernel-switching is happening mid-batch (GPU context churn).

maya: pasting the critical snippet:```
# kernel metrics sample
batch_size=24, seq=512, kv_used=11.4GB, kernel=flash_attn_v2, fallback=matmul_slow
context_switches=2, avg_kernel_ms=5.8 -> 9.6 during spike
```

leo: that avg_kernel_ms delta suggests we hit a slower execution path. maybe because memory layout forced us off the optimized kernels. if KV footprint grows beyond a threshold we route to fallback kernels.

ash: related: our continuous-batcher admission currently uses a token_budget_per_batch target of 12k tokens for that model. when queueing saturates we still try to keep batch width which increases kv allocations per batch.

maya: exact. I think it's two-fold: (1) batch formation tries to maximize token throughput and doesn't account for KV page fragmentation, (2) queue policy holds requests to meet token targets, which spikes ephemeral KV footprint.

ash: proposed quick mitigation: reduce token_budget_per_batch for KV-heavy models to 7k and enable preemptive-mini-batch flush when node headroom < 12%.

ash: config example:```{"continuous_batching": {"token_budget_target": 7000, "max_hold_ms": 35, "preemptive_flush_headroom_pct": 12}}```

leo: what about a softer reservation for pinned KV? like a per-request soft_kv_reserve so we don't overcommit when many requests with long histories land concurrently. could be a small delta per request that prevents admission when aggregated > node_kv_headroom.

ash: yes, soft_kv_reserve sounds useful. basically treat N pinned tokens as extra weight. admission check becomes: for candidate batch sum(req.soft_kv_reserve) + current_kv_usage <= headroom_limit.

maya: we should also consider kernel-switch penalty in the batching heuristic. if a batch mixes short and long sequences that triggers a kernel route change, cost goes up. maybe prefer homogenous batches when headroom is tight.

ash: agree. heuristic: when headroom < 20% prefer same-seq-length grouping and cap batch_token_target to 60% of usual. fallback: if we can't fill within max_hold_ms, flush.

sophia: any profiling evidence that homogenous batches avoid kernel switches?

maya: yes — on the flamegraphs, mixed batches show duplicated kernel invocations and extra memcpy calls. homogenous runs show ~12% less kernel time for same token count.

perf-bot: [note] experiment suggestion created: exp/mini-window-homogeneous-3058765432 (A/B traffic split 10/90).

leo: longer-term: could we add a KV-aware admission scoring function used by the batch assembler? score = alpha*expected_tokens + beta*kv_footprint + gamma*kernel_penalty_estimate. tune weights per model.

ash: that fits the Optimize roadmap. for immediate rollout, I can push the reduced token_budget + preemptive flush change behind a kill-switch for the affected model group. low-risk toggle.

maya: ok please run a quick canary: reduce to 7k token target on two nodes, route 5% traffic for 30m, capture p50/p95, kv headroom, kernel switch counts.

ash: on it. creating rollout:```deployctl rollout --target=nodeset:kv-legacy --cfg token_budget_target=7000 --canary=0.05 --dur 30m --tag mini-window-kv-safety```

sophia: add extra tracing for kernel_route decisions and per-request kv_reserve field so we can analyze admission failures.

ash: will add trace fields. also enabling perf-bot alerts for >2 kernel switches per batch.

maya: if we see too many preemptive flushes hurting throughput, we should try a dynamic headroom threshold: start at 12% but increase to 18% if we detect pipeline stalls upstream.

leo: one gotcha — preemptive flush increases number of smaller kernels calls which can increase overhead. we need to balance latency vs p95 tail.

maya: agreed. that's why canary and A/B are needed. goal is p95 drop back to baseline without >6% throughput loss.

perf-bot: [result placeholder] will post canary metrics at 3058765900.

ash: quick note to docs team: I'll add a short section in runtime/continuous-batcher.md describing kv-aware admission and config knobs.

maya: thanks. follow-ups: (1) ash runs canary and posts profiler (flamegraphs + kernel switch counts), (2) leo prototypes soft_kv_reserve estimator, (3) sophia wires tracing. check back in ~45m. :thumbsup:

leo: copying the estimator idea — will drop a PR with test harness.

ash: canary started. posting first snapshot in ~5m.

maya: great, thanks everyone.
